source.citation: Tsukrov, I. and Kachanov, M. (2000). Effective moduli of an anisotropic material with elliptical holes of arbitrary orientational distribution. International Journal of Solids and Structures 37(41), 5919-5941.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF), captions and equations read on the page images
transcription.note: The orthotropic matrix of the three figures is given by ratios only: E1/E2 = 4.1, E1/G12 = 10, nu12 = 0.277 and nu21 = 0.068 (= 0.277/4.1 to its rounding). The plate is two-dimensional, in plane stress. The figures plot E1/E2 for randomly oriented elliptical holes: against the area fraction p for b/a = 1, 1/2 and 1/4 (Fig. 5), against b/a at fixed crack densities rho = 0.05 and 0.1 of the major axes (Fig. 6), and against b/a at fixed p = 0.2 and 0.3 (Fig. 7); the curves are not transcribed, the page recomputes them and sets them against Eq. (44).

E1_over_E2.description: Ratio of the Young moduli of the matrix along and across its stiff axis.

E1_over_G12.description: Ratio of the Young modulus along the stiff axis to the shear modulus of the matrix.

nu12.description: Poisson ratio nu12 of the matrix.

nu21.description: Poisson ratio nu21 of the matrix, nu12 E2/E1 rounded.

figure_settings.curves: rho = 0.05, 0.1 (density of the major axes, sum of a^2 over A)

notes: E1/E2 of the matrix is 4.1, the value at p = 0 of Fig. 5.
